transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-11-11 10:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood CSM); Rajiv (CTO), Maya (Platform), Leah (Security), Daniel (DevOps), Priya (PM)

Summary:
Quick sync on Private/VPC pilot  networking blockers still top priority, did a run-through of recent upgrade, saw tail latency regression on one worker, discussed routing fallback and KMS test plan. Agreement to share docs and run targeted perf tests this week.

Topics:
- Networking / VPC peering / firewall rules
- Routing & routing policies between regions (primary -> failover)
- Recent runtime upgrade (v2.1.4) and observed behavior
- KMS integration and audit logs
- Next steps and pilot expansion pricing

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time. quick agenda  network status, upgrade notes, perf results, then next steps.
[00:18] Rajiv: yeah thanks, we only have 45 so i'll be brief, main ask is we need the VPC peering pattern that works for our restricted subnets, and also clear firewall ports.
[00:35] Ethan: absolutely, we pushed a new control-plane bootstrap doc last night but note it's a draft; we'll walk through specifics now.
[00:50] Maya: quick heads up  when we tried the peering yesterday, the health checks from the private control plane to our ingress failed intermittently, sometimes fine, sometimes 502s.
[01:05] Ethan: okay, that sounds like either an MTU or an idle timeout on the egress NAT path; did you see any packet drops on the host routes?
[01:15] Daniel: we saw increased RSTs on the NAT gateway during the test window, logs attached to the ticket (link).
[01:27] Sophia: sorry sofia 
[01:30] Sofia: no worries, thanks daniel. Ethan can you remind us the ports we expect open both directions?
[01:40] Ethan: yep  control plane <-> node comms is TCP 443 for the API plus UDP 514 for logs (optional), and we also recommend allowing ephemeral ports for healthcheck callbacks. We'll send a one-pager with CIDR examples.
[01:52] Leah: on security side we'll need explicit justification for the ephemeral ranges; otherwise we prefer a NAT only pattern and explicit proxy. Also want to confirm KMS envelope encryption flow.
[02:05] Ethan: KMS flow is: customer KMS issues key -> Redwood uses it for disk/secret encryption, we don't export keys. For the pilot we tested a mock KMS flow and logged successful encrypt/decrypt; we'll share the call traces.
[02:20] Rajiv: that's good but our policy requires HSM-backed keys and a proof-of-concept for key rotation. can redwood demonstrate rotation without downtime?
[02:34] Sofia: yes, rotation is non-disruptive  we staged rotation on the dev cluster last month. Ethan can share the runbook.
[02:42] Ethan: i'll attach the rotation runbook and the test logs.
[02:48] Maya: switching to the runtime upgrade  we moved to v2.1.4 yesterday as you recommended. overall throughput improved but we saw a p99 tail spike on worker-3 around 10:12 UTC.
[03:04] Ethan: that's the behavior we wanted to dig into; do you have the profiler traces?
[03:10] Maya: yes uploaded, although the trace names got munged by the collector so some function names are off.
[03:18] Ethan: that's okay  common with our collector config, we'll correlate by span IDs. prelim notes: the spike aligned with a KV cache miss and a cold-start of the attention CUDA kernel on that worker.
[03:34] Daniel: are you suggesting we need a warmup job or patch the kernel selection for that model?
[03:40] Ethan: both are options. we have a warmup job we can run during off-peak, and we can also force the runtime to pre-select a quantized kernel variant which reduces cold-start time but might change latency distribution slightly.
[03:54] Rajiv: what about accuracy regressions when forcing quantized kernels? we need to know tradeoffs.
[04:02] Ethan: for our tests on your model family, 4-bit quant with per-channel calibration had negligible accuracy diffs on the eval set you provided; we'll send the eval spreadsheet. 8-bit is even safer.
[04:16] Leah: please include the prompt set and evaluation metrics in that sheet, need to show to security/compliance.
[04:24] Sofia: noted  Ethan will include variant metrics.
[04:28] Carlos: quick commercial note  if you want to expand to 2x capacity during pilot we'll give a short-term discount, i'll follow up with numbers.
[04:38] Priya: thanks carlos, budgeting is tight but we might scale if perf is solid.
[04:44] Sofia: back to networking  Maya, can you confirm whether the 502s were during burst load?
[04:51] Maya: yes correlated with a burst from our QA runners hitting 200 concurrent sessions. single-request latency was fine but concurrency exposed the worker queueing.
[04:59] Ethan: sounds like batching policy needs tuning; we can lower max batch size and increase throughput threads to reduce queueing under burst. that will slightly increase per-token compute overhead but reduce p99 latency.
[05:14] Rajiv: what's the configuration change surface? low-level flags or a config in the deploy?
[05:20] Ethan: it's a runtime config we can apply per-deployment; no code change. we'll propose three profiles (low-latency, balanced, cost-optimized) and you can choose.
[05:30] Daniel: what about routing failover? if primary region blips we need deterministic fallback to our EU region without draining requests.
[05:39] Ethan: we support policy-based routing; for the pilot we suggested active-passive with sticky session fallback. If you want active-active we can discuss sticky hashing to maintain KV cache locality, but that adds cross-region KV replication complexity.
[05:56] Rajiv: active-passive is fine for now. ensure SLOs for failover are documented.
[06:02] Leah: also ensure audit logs for failed routing events are forwarded into our SIEM.
[06:09] Ethan: yes, audit events stream over syslog and can be forwarded to your Splunk/SIEM; we'll send config examples.
[06:16] Sofia: quick checkpoint  agreed items: send network one-pager, rotation runbook, kernel/quant results, and pricing.
[06:24] [small crosstalk]
[06:30] Maya: one more question on telemetry retention  will Redwood keep detailed traces or just aggregated metrics?
[06:36] Carlos: default is 30 days for traces, 90 days for aggregates in pilot; extended retention is an add-on.
[06:45] Leah: for compliance we need at least 90 days of traces for the pilot evaluation. is that possible?
[06:51] Carlos: we can enable 90 days for the pilot at no extra charge for the first month, will confirm in email.
[06:59] Priya: timeline check  we're slated to make a pilot go/no-go decision by 2027-11-30.
[07:06] Rajiv: yes, need the perf numbers and KMS proof before that.
[07:12] Ethan: action: i'll send the kv/cache warmup script and a recommended warmup schedule, plus the quantization eval.
[07:20] Daniel: i'll run the ingress perf test and post results.
[07:25] Leah: i'll validate KMS flow and confirm rotation gaps.
[07:30] Sofia: perfect. any blockers besides the NAT/peering flakiness?
[07:36] Maya: not from infra, just need the exact CIDR examples  our infra team is strict about naming and we want no overlap.
[07:44] Sofia: we'll include recommended prefixes and a sample terraform snippet in the network doc.
[07:51] Carlos: i'll send a short pilot expansion price sheet by Monday.
[07:56] Priya: can we get the control plane demo recording too? that helped the execs last week.
[08:02] Sofia: yes, will share the recording and the slide deck.
[08:07] [wrap-up]
[08:12] Sofia: recap of next steps and owners. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts: speaker labels sometimes abbreviated; a few proper nouns (KMS vendor name) were misheard in the recorder.
